text:
maya: alerting — 99p latency jump on gpool-7 starting ~1954321000, correlated with streaming backpressure and elevated queue lengths
deploy-bot: [ALERT] streaming-backpressure-high gpool-7 (service=inference-runtime)
maya: graphs show a sharp increase in tail latency and a backlog of partial streams, not just new requests
ryan: any noisy tenant IDs in the logs? can we correlate with tenant routing?
maya: quick grep shows a cluster of requests from tenant t-42 with many tool-calls, prompt lengths vary wildly (400-12000 tokens)
sanjay: that sounds like a tool-calling loop — we've seen long prompt churn + tool replies cause KV blowout and kernel misselection before
jie: pulled a profile for a stressed worker: kernel selector switched to dense-matmul fallback for ~25% of steps, causing 2-3x token latencies
maya: logs snippet: ```kernel_selector: chose=fallback_dense reason=seq_len_estimate mismatch kv_cache_size=1.9GB evictions=78```
alex: why is kernel_selector mispredicting seq_len? are we using last-request heuristic?
sanjay: yes, selector uses recent mean seq_len for heuristic. sudden tail in prompt length from t-42 can skew it and pick kernels optimized for long context, but then many requests are short — leads to poor throughput
ryan: also seeing repeated KV cache evictions in same worker which triggers costly recompute of KV and rebuild of streaming contexts
maya: batching heuristics note: autoscaling bumped batch size up due to throughput signal, combined with streaming partials blocked headroom -> backpressure cascade
ops-bot: FYI reclaim:ed 2 workers from gpool-7 due to oom risk, flagged tenant t-42 as high I/O
alex: mitigation idea: temporarily enforce per-tenant max-ongoing-streams=8 and cap batch size on gpool-7 to 16 to relieve head-of-line blocking
sanjay: agree. also propose fast-path kernel override for streams <1k tokens: force kernels with small-init latency to avoid dense fallback
jie: can we patch kernel selector to use percentile (95p) instead of mean for seq_len estimation? might be more robust to spikes
maya: rolling patch candidate: set selector.window=300s, estimator=95p, and add per-tenant stream cap; want to test on gpool-7 canary
ryan: perf regression risk: changing estimator could slightly increase cost for some workloads — need A/B on canary and cost telemetry
maya: ran a small canary with these changes on gpool-7-iz1 — tail latency dropped ~45% in 10m window, KV evictions halved, streaming backlog cleared
alex: nice. what's the plan to roll to prod? full rollout plus config guard rails? or staged by pool?
sanjay: staged by pool with automatic rollback if 99p > baseline *1.3 for 5m. Also add short-term tenant throttling for t-42 while we notify customer success
maya: CS ping: @cs-team — heads up, we'll throttle t-42 for 2 hours to stabilize. will follow up with findings and suggested replay for their workflow
jie: logging follow-up: add a lightweight marker when kernel_selector overrides are applied and emit reason codes; helps debugging recurrence
ops-bot: scheduled job: apply canary to gpool-7-prod at 1954321500, rollback window 15m
maya: action items: 1) deploy selector params to canary (assigned: sanjay) 2) set per-tenant stream cap (assigned: ryan) 3) add selector debug logs (assigned: jie) 4) notify CS (assigned: maya)
ryan: I'll also add a temporary queue-depth alarm per-pool to catch similar pressure earlier
maya: thanks all, monitoring looks stable so far after canary. will keep thread updated
alex: great response — please file a short post-incident note with kernel selector root cause + config defaults to avoid this in new clusters
maya: will do, creating doc in #incidents after stabilization :thumbsup:
__note: Per agents.md, Slack threads are a single string of messages with names prefixed. All fields are strings or list of strings.
